scenario: A climate summit invites delegates if they have either elite climate-science expertise or elite negotiation skill. A 5% wildcard also invites people with neither trait. Organizers think science expertise and negotiation skill are negatively related among invitees.

data.description: Invitation is based on either trait plus a wildcard.

question: Among invitees, compute (a) P(science | negotiation, selected), and (b) P(science | not negotiation, selected). Is the negative association real or induced by selection?

ground_truth.explanation: The traits are independent in the population, but selection on either trait induces a spurious negative association.

naive_answer: Science expertise and negotiation skill appear negatively related among invitees, so the two capabilities likely trade off.
naive_trap: The summit invitation rule creates collider bias.
